en-US.description: AI usage and quota monitoring in the Windows system tray.
en-US.name: TideSI
en-US.releaseNotes:
Changes
- Add native dms package to flake.nix (#97)
- Add hermetic provider E2E coverage and clarify unavailable spend (#95)
- Cosmic host (#96)
- Let providers be reordered by dragging in Settings → Providers (#94)
- Zed usage (#93)
- Run the macOS CI on macos-15; GitHub is retiring the macos-14 image
- Run pre-commit tools via dev-tool.sh so hooks work with or without Nix
- Fix provider refresh, recover local spend, and add DMS Quickshell integration (#86)
- fix(claude): read Remote Control sessions from CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (#92)
- fix(claude): read settings, stats and transcripts from CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (#91)
- refactor(kiro): share one SQLite item reader and test both usage formats (#90)
- Fix Kiro IDE nested usage snapshot detection (#89)
- fix ci windows cli background
- fix(tests): derive expected dates from the local timezone (#88)
- homebrew: tidesi 4.0.1
- scoop: tidesi 4.0.1
- fix: i118
- fix badges
Install by downloading the .plasmoid file and running:
plasmapkg2 -i tidesi-4.1.0.plasmoid
Windows: run tideSI-Setup-4.1.0.exe (no admin rights needed; it updates an existing install in place). Or unzip tideSI-windows-4.1.0.zip anywhere and run tideSI.exe. Either way it lives in the tray.
Stable Windows builds also include Scoop and WinGet manifests. See the package manager instructions.
macOS: open tidesi-macos-4.1.0-apple-silicon.dmg (M1 and later) or tidesi-macos-4.1.0-intel.dmg (Intel Macs; Apple menu → About This Mac → Chip/Processor says which) and drag Tidesi.app to Applications (ZIPs also available). It lives in the menu bar. If macOS blocks the first launch, use System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. See the macOS install guide.
All platform assets are attached a few minutes after the release appears, once their build has passed.
